whatIsSealing.title: What Is Ultrasonic Sealing?
whatIsSealing.description: Ultrasonic sealing uses high-frequency mechanical vibration to join compatible materials through localized heat generated at the joining area. For ID card lanyard applications, the process can be used to secure the lanyard and attachment arrangement into a finished assembly.
whatIsSealing.factorsTitle: The exact sealing method depends on:
whatIsSealing.footnote: The objective is to create a cleaner and more finished lanyard attachment.

whyUseSealing.title: Why Use Ultrasonic Sealing?
whyUseSealing.lede: Traditional lanyard assemblies can use exposed metal attachment components. Ultrasonic sealing provides an alternative attachment method that reduces dependence on exposed metal attachment points in suitable configurations.
whyUseSealing.hardwareIssuesTitle: Depending on the design and environment, exposed metal hardware may:

advantages.title: A More Finished Appearance
advantages.body: The sealed connection can create a cleaner-looking transition between the lanyard and attachment.

advantages.title: Reduced Exposure to Sharp Metal Parts
advantages.body: Where the selected configuration allows it, ultrasonic sealing can reduce the amount of exposed metal hardware around the attachment area.

advantages.title: Better Long-Term Appearance
advantages.body: Because the attachment can be integrated into the lanyard assembly, it can avoid some of the appearance issues associated with exposed metal hardware.

warningBox.title: Important:
warningBox.text: Ultrasonic sealing does not make every lanyard or attachment configuration permanently corrosion-proof. Its suitability depends on the materials and construction used.

items.q: What is ultrasonic sealing in a lanyard?
items.a: Ultrasonic sealing is a joining process used to securely attach a lanyard to an attachment component such as a hook, holder, clip or other fitting. It creates a clean, stitchless connection between the lanyard material and the selected attachment.

items.q: What is ultrasonic sealing used for in lanyard manufacturing?
items.a: At iDGen, ultrasonic sealing is used to join the lanyard with its selected attachment hardware. This can include hooks, holders, clips and other suitable attachment components required for identification or event lanyards.

items.q: Can a lanyard be joined to a hook using ultrasonic sealing?
items.a: Yes. Ultrasonic sealing can be used to join a lanyard to a suitable hook attachment, creating a clean finished connection without conventional stitching or a separate metal clamp.

items.q: Can ultrasonic sealing be used with ID card holders?
items.a: Yes. Where the holder and lanyard configuration is suitable, ultrasonic sealing can be used to connect the lanyard to the holder or its attachment point.

items.q: Can ultrasonic sealing be used with different lanyard attachments?
items.a: Yes. Depending on the lanyard design and attachment hardware, ultrasonic sealing can be used with suitable hooks, holders, clips and other compatible attachment components. The joining method depends on the materials and construction of the selected components.

items.q: What is the advantage of ultrasonic sealing over stitching?
items.a: Ultrasonic sealing creates a stitchless connection between the lanyard and attachment component. It provides a clean and consistent finished appearance without visible sewing thread at the joined area.

items.q: What are the benefits of using ultrasonic sealing instead of a metal clamp?
items.a: Ultrasonic sealing can eliminate the need for a separate metal clamp at the lanyard attachment point. This can provide a cleaner finish and avoids a metal component that may develop surface corrosion or rust over time, particularly when exposed to moisture. For products worn by students or other users around the neck, avoiding exposed metal at the attachment point can also reduce the possibility of sharp or corroded edges causing discomfort or minor injury.

items.q: Does ultrasonic sealing make the lanyard attachment stronger?
items.a: Ultrasonic sealing creates a fused connection designed to securely join suitable lanyard material and attachment components. The final strength depends on the lanyard material, attachment type, construction and manufacturing settings.

items.q: Can custom printed lanyards be supplied with ultrasonic-sealed attachments?
items.a: Yes. Custom printed lanyards can be produced with suitable attachment components and ultrasonic sealing. Organizations can specify their preferred lanyard design, branding and attachment configuration during the quotation process.

items.q: Can ultrasonic-sealed lanyards be used for schools, companies and events?
items.a: Yes. Ultrasonic-sealed lanyard assemblies can be supplied for schools, colleges, universities, companies, institutions, conferences, exhibitions, events, membership programmes and other identification requirements.

items.q: Can I order lanyards with ultrasonic sealing but without an ID card?
items.a: Yes. Lanyards can be ordered separately with the required attachment and ultrasonic-sealed connection. An ID card does not need to be included in the order.

items.q: What information is required to order an ultrasonic-sealed lanyard?
items.a: Provide the lanyard width and material, required quantity, printing or branding requirements, preferred attachment such as hook or holder, and any specific finishing requirements. iDGen can confirm the suitable attachment and ultrasonic-sealing configuration for the project.
